name: R2D3 — A Visual Introduction to Machine Learning
oneLine: Scrollytelling decision-tree explainer: light Helvetica narrative left, one persistent chart morphing on the right as you scroll.

palette.note: Pure white page, no section fills
Body copy in light Helvetica; titles in #000000
Green class: San Francisco homes, dots rendered at partial opacity
Navy class: New York homes; overlap of the two creates the visual density
10px axis tick labels like '$293.0 per sqft'

type.note: Title 60px weight 300, ~-2% tracking, tight ~1.1 leading, three stacked lines; H2 48px light with a 3px black rule beneath
21px weight 300, ~1.5 line-height; key terms bumped to weight 700 ('statistical learning', 'scatterplot')
10-11px regular gray axis labels and 'SCROLL' cue in bold caps with a downward triangle

layout: Two-column split at 1440px: ~460px text column starting at x=150, chart occupies the right ~55% and stays pinned while text scrolls.
Huge vertical gaps (300-400px) between text blocks so each step gets its own scroll beat; chart is often the only thing on screen.
On mobile the split is kept, so the chart is cropped off the right edge and text squeezes to ~270px (weak responsive story).
motion: Scroll-driven transitions: the same ~400 data points re-layout from scatterplot matrix to 1-D elevation strip to histogram bars as sections advance (visible across screenshots).
(inferred) Points tween positions with eased D3 transitions over ~1s, preserving object constancy so you can track a home from one chart to the next.
(inferred) Later sections grow a decision tree branch by branch with points flowing down the splits; won Kantar Information is Beautiful gold for this.
interactions: Scroll is the primary interaction: position in the narrative drives the chart state.
Language selector dropdown in the hero; 'Keep scrolling' italic cue plus SCROLL arrow.
steal: Model-pipeline section: one pinned chart of telemetry points that morphs (raw channels -> embedding scatter -> anomaly histogram) as the left-column copy advances.
Class encoding: two semi-transparent hues (nominal vs anomalous) so overlap density itself becomes the story in our scatter/UMAP view.
Hero typography: very light, large, tightly tracked display weight stacked over 3 lines, paired with 21px light body, for an Apple-like calm.
leave: The non-responsive split on mobile (chart cropped off-screen); our scrolly sections must restack to chart-on-top on 390px.
Default browser select and dated 2015 chrome (boxed R2D3 logo, triangle arrow) undercut a modern polish bar.
